   167	
   168	A trusted **canary** (helper image) runs first in an identical container. It asserts:
   169	- only the `lo` interface exists under `/sys/class/net`, which proves no network rather than inferring it from a failed connection;
   170	- no Docker socket;
   171	- UID 10001;
   172	- `/work` is read-only;
   173	- no host paths visible.
   174	
   175	Repository code never runs as part of the self-test.
   176	
   177	#### 5.1.5 Collecting results (ATLAS-D04)
   178	- Collection starts **only after** every container of the execution has been confirmed stopped (§5.1.7).
   179	- Only `/out` is collected. `/work` and the writable areas are never copied to the host; source attestation happens in the VM.
   180	- `/out` is streamed as a tar (`docker cp <ctr>:/out -`) into ATLAS's extractor. The extractor uses Python's `tarfile` with `filter="data"` plus stricter rules:
   181	  - it accepts **regular files and directories only**, rejecting symlinks, hardlinks, FIFOs and devices;
   182	  - it rejects absolute paths and `..`;
   183	  - it enforces limits: total bytes, file count, per-file size and a deadline;
   184	  - it extracts into a fresh `0700` directory, never following links (`O_NOFOLLOW`).
   185	
   186	  Anything that violates these rules discards the collection and marks the run `invalid_output`.
   187	
   188	#### 5.1.6 Network (ATLAS-D09)
   189	- **Tests: `--network none`, always**, in this release. `tests.network` (integration tests needing the network) is **not available**; enabling it needs a new decision.
   190	- **Dependency setup** may use the **egress profile**, a per-project opt-in approved by the user. The setup container joins an `internal: true` Docker network whose only peer is an ATLAS-owned **egress proxy** (helper image). The proxy:
   191	  - allows only the project's approved registry hosts (e.g. `pypi.org`, `files.pythonhosted.org`, `registry.npmjs.org`) on 443;
   192	  - denies host, gateway, link-local, RFC1918 and Colima host-gateway addresses after DNS resolution.
   193	
   194	  ATLAS verifies the effective policy in the canary: an allowed host is reachable, and the host gateway and a LAN address are not. Setup runs with source read-only and only the dependency volumes writable, and installer lifecycle scripts run inside that same contract.
   195	- **VM-escape exposure, stated accurately.** A container or runtime escape reaches the ATLAS VM: its disk, which holds other executions' volumes, and its network, which can reach the macOS host through the VM gateway. Mitigations:
   196	  - no host mounts;
   197	  - execution volumes are deleted after each run, so at most concurrent executions' volumes are exposed (one per repository by default);
   198	  - nothing ATLAS-sensitive listens on the host network except the dashboard on `127.0.0.1`, which requires the session token.
   199	
   200	  This is a residual risk (R16), not "nothing is reachable".
   201	
   202	#### 5.1.7 Lifecycle and recovery (ATLAS-D07)
   203	- Container and volume names are deterministic (`atlas-<execution_id>-<role>`, `src-<execution_id>`, …). They are **persisted on the execution row before `docker create`**.
   204	- On timeout, pause, cancel and restart, ATLAS:
   205	  1. lists every container labelled `atlas.execution_id=<id>`;
   206	  2. runs `docker kill`, then `docker wait`/`inspect` until none is running;
   207	  3. collects (§5.1.5);
   208	  4. removes containers and volumes.
   209	
   210	  Host process-group exit of the `docker` CLI is **not** treated as quiescence. If the daemon is unreachable, the run goes to `BLOCKED(sandbox_state_unknown)`, and no evidence is accepted until the containers are confirmed gone.
   211	- Startup reconciliation (recovery-strategy.md §3 step 3) includes orphaned `atlas.*`-labelled containers and volumes.
   212	
   213	#### 5.1.8 Resource containment (ATLAS-D08)
   214	- Bounded: memory, CPU, PIDs, `tmpfs` sizes, log size, collection bytes and file counts, wall-clock time.
   215	- Persistent writes (dependency volumes, `/out`) are measured by the helper during the run (`du` on the volumes, polled). Exceeding the project's storage limit kills the execution (`failed(resource_limit)`).
   216	- The ATLAS VM disk is separate and size-capped, so exhaustion can't fill the macOS disk or `~/.atlas`.
   217	
   218	#### 5.1.9 Who can reach Docker (ATLAS-D05)
   219	Hiding the socket isn't enough, because any process running as the user can connect to a user-owned Unix socket. So:
   220	- **Agent processes run inside an ATLAS outer Seatbelt wrapper** (`sandbox-exec`; this is unrelated to the test sandbox). It denies file access to `~/.colima`, `~/.docker`, `~/.atlas` (except the agent's own worktree) and `/var/run/docker.sock`, and denies `network-outbound` to Unix sockets under those paths.

The spike adds a test where an agent-launched command tries `curl --unix-socket ~/.colima/atlas/docker.sock` and must fail.

   223	- The test sandbox containers have no socket (§5.1.4).
   224	
   225	#### 5.1.10 Fail closed
   226	G-TEST can't pass, and the project shows `BLOCKED(no_test_sandbox)`, if any of these hold:
   227	- Colima `atlas` isn't running;
   228	- the VM has host mounts;
   229	- an image digest isn't approved;
   230	- attestation, the canary or the contract check fails;
   231	- the repository has an unsupported feature (§5.1.2).
   232	
   233	The UI tells the user exactly what to run. ATLAS doesn't start or reconfigure the VM itself until Phase 10 (launchd).
   234	
   235	#### 5.1.11 Limits
   236	- **macOS toolchains:** projects that need Xcode, Swift for iOS/macOS or macOS-only binaries can't be tested in Linux containers. They get `BLOCKED(no_test_sandbox)`. The earlier Seatbelt test profile is kept on file as a fallback that needs a separate decision per project. It is **not** enabled.
   237	- **Source mutation:** projects whose tests write to tracked files are unsupported (§5.1.3).
   238	- **Submodules and LFS** are unsupported (§5.1.2).
   239	- **Playwright/browser tests** (Phase 7) use the pinned Playwright image, with the app started in the same container. `--network none` still allows localhost.
   240	
   241	### 5.2 Agent processes
   242	- **Codex** `-s read-only` / `workspace-write` uses Codex's Seatbelt sandbox for the commands it runs. **To verify in Phase 2:** whether Codex sandboxed commands can *read* outside the workspace (e.g. `~/.atlas/atlas.db`, other projects' worktrees). If they can, this is **cross-project read exposure**, and ATLAS will mitigate it by:
   243	  - (a) running the agent through the same Seatbelt profile wrapper (outer sandbox) with read access to the worktree plus the provider's own config dir, or
   244	  - (b) the dedicated-user mechanism.
   245	
   246	  The provider CLI must be able to read its own auth, and that is inherent. It must not be able to read ATLAS state or other projects.
   247	- **Claude Code**: permission modes and allowlists are enforced inside the CLI, not by the OS. `Read`/`Grep`/`Glob` are scoped to the working directories, and `dontAsk` denies the rest. **To verify in Phase 2:** enabling Claude Code's OS-level sandbox ([docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sandboxing)) via `--settings` for any role that has Bash.    250	### 5.3 Other
   251	- Worktrees isolate *git state*, not *processes*. Process isolation comes only from §5.1/§5.2.
